objective: `stockroom/csvio.py` holds the reader and writer of three unrelated file formats (item catalogue, stock levels, orders) and a helper they share. Split it by file format into three new modules, `stockroom/items_csv.py`, `stockroom/stock_csv.py` and `stockroom/orders_csv.py`, keep `stockroom/csvio.py` as the place callers import from, and make sure the shared whole-number helper exists once and is not copied into each new module. Move the code as it is: every reader and writer behaves exactly as before, including its error messages, and the existing tests keep passing without being edited.
acceptance: `items_csv` defines `ITEM_HEADER`, `parse_tags`, `read_items` and `write_items`; `stock_csv` defines `STOCK_HEADER` and `read_stock`; `orders_csv` defines `ORDER_HEADER`, `read_orders` and `write_orders`; the `__module__` of each function is its new module

`csvio` exports exactly these nine names, lists them in `__all__`, and each is the same object as in the module that defines it; `csvio.py` itself holds only its docstring, imports and `__all__`, no definitions of its own
`items_csv`, `stock_csv` and `orders_csv` do not import `csvio` and do not import each other
The code that turns a cell into a whole number or raises the `... is not a whole number: ...` error exists exactly once in the `stockroom` package

`read_items`, `read_stock` and `read_orders` return the same result, or raise the same exception class with the same message (line numbers included), as before for the same text: empty input and blank lines, padded and wrong headers, rows with too few or too many fields, bad or negative numbers, bad SKUs, dates and statuses, CRLF line endings, a missing final newline, repeated order ids, empty rows, and quoted fields in an order file, including the order in which several problems in one file are reported

`write_items` and `write_orders` produce the same text as before (including quoting of cells with commas and of prices from 1,000.00 in orders) and `read_items(write_items(x))` and `read_orders(write_orders(x))` return `x`
`from stockroom.csvio import *` exposes exactly the nine names, and `scripts/make_sample_data.py` writes byte-identical files for the same seed and order count
